quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching the intersection where you are driving. It has its siren on and lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, finish crossing and then move to the right side of the road and stop. You must yield to all police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep the roadways safe. If you abuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
One at the top and one at the bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: A child is about to run into the street in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Honk your horn loudly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn loudly.
questions.explanation: Use a loud horn blast when a child or any pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle. This warns them of danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane to keep traffic moving.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for passing or turning left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic around you, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: When is pavement most slippery and dangerous?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain has just started.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain has just started.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the pavement mix with the water, creating a slick coating.

questions.question: The MVA will suspend your license if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.
0.06 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: When you drive in Maryland, you agree to a blood alcohol test. The MVA will suspend your license if the test shows a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
After you clear the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough space to safely pull in front of the other vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The roadway ends ahead.
You must go either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must go either right or left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road splits and you must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow warning sign with black markings. It warns you that the divided highway is ending. Be ready to change lanes or move your position.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk or sidewalk area when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection, what must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, check for oncoming traffic or pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: Look toward the center of the roadway.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming driver's headlights are too bright. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road so you can stay in your lane. Do not flash your bright lights back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign says you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers which laws they must follow. They are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols. They inform drivers about direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking, and special rules.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?

options.text: Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match the flow of traffic.
Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.
Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Speed up only after you have found a gap in traffic on the interstate. Wait while stopped until you see a safe gap before speeding up and merging.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire suddenly goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using the brakes gently.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning when driving in the rain?

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water. This occurs when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slow down when it is raining or wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes if your vehicle is skidding. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up or drops off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop no matter which direction you are driving.
Stop only if you are driving the same direction as the bus.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop no matter which direction you are driving.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children. You must stop from any direction you are traveling.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, remove your foot from the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is sliding. If you have anti-lock brakes, press the brakes firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What might the truck do?

options.text: Complete the turn in either of the two lanes.
Swing wide to complete the right turn.
Stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more space to turn because the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. This difference is greater for longer vehicles. Long trucks often swing wide to complete a right turn safely.

questions.question: If it feels like your tires lost contact with the road, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before you stop or turn.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle could be stopped on the road ahead. Slow down when you approach a hill or curve so you can stop if necessary.
